sentences.text: Lonchodectes is a genus of pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous of England, primarily found near Kent.
This animal possessed long jaws with many short teeth that were compressed vertically, resembling a pair of sugar tongs.
At least some species of Lonchodectes had crests on their lower jaw.
The type species Lonchodectes compressirostris is based on a partial upper jaw fossil found in the Upper Cretaceous Upper Chalk near Kent.
The genus Lonchodectes was named by Hooley in 1914.
There are 9 recorded fossil occurrences of Lonchodectes.
Unwin considered Lonchodectes a generalist species similar to a gull due to its conservative jaws and teeth, estimating a maximum wingspan of nearly 2 meters.
Recent studies suggest that Lonchodectes had limb proportions similar to azdarchids and may have lived in a similar way.
Lonchodectes belongs to the parent group Ornithocheiroidea.
Lonchodectes is classified within the class Reptilia.
In 2003, the genus was placed in the family Lonchodectidae within Ctenochasmatoidea, and later in 2006, it was placed within Azhdarchoidea.
Recent reviews have limited the genus Lonchodectes to only its type species, L. compressirostris.
Lonchodectes lived from the Albian to the Turonian stages, between 113.2 and 89.8 million years ago.
It is debated whether Lonchodectes is a valid genus, as species were previously assigned to Ornithocheirus until the work of David Unwin.
The status of L. platystomus is debated, with some suggesting it may belong to the genus Amblydectes.
In 2019, researchers suggested that the type specimen of Lonchodectes compressirostris might be the same species as Cimoliopterus cuvieri.
